items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Charlie "Dizzie" Lewis liked his juice although he did not drink too much while we were in Bombay.

ctx.x: One thing I had a hard time to get used to was Lizards. They were everywhere and in the best hotels and houses. In our place they were almost as thick as flies, our beds had screens to protect us from mosquitos, but there was no protection to keep lizards out of the house. They were about two-and-a-half inches long with tails almost twice as long as the body and are known as wall lizards. Whenever we did use the stove in the kitchen, we had to light it and leave the oven door open so that the lizards would get…

I drank less alcohol in India than I was drinking in Europe and I suppose the desire was less demanding because of the climate, although hot climates have been known to make alcoholic wrecks of many men. We had plenty of canned beer that was furnished to us by the hotel. For a woman, Aimee Denton could down a few. Leon liked a taste of gage now and then and Charlie "Dizzie" Lewis liked his juice although he did not drink too much while we were in Bombay.

But one day Dizzie got on a bender and bought a python from an Indian who had a street act for tourists which was a battle between a snake and a mongoose. So Dizzy bought a python and took it home. His girl friends Ivy was not at home when he arrived. In fact no one was there and the juice started getting Dizzy down, so he got on a bed with the python and went to sleep.
